answers.assumption_check: Load-bearing: the 100 blank-owner PROVED tickets each have a component charter that owns them. Measured false for at least 94e1cce8941e, which settled a decision record. So the plan allows a recorded no-charter finding per ticket rather than forcing a fill, and each such finding becomes a question to Akien if the store needs a value. A second assumption is that the cast door already refuses a blank owner on new casts (transitions.py:2227 lists owning_intention among the required fields), so this population is legacy and does not regrow.
answers.builder_check: A Haiku builder needs to know: (1) where the list comes from: tickets under CairnCommons/tickets/ whose workflow_and_state shows [PROVED] and whose owning_intention is blank; (2) what to read per ticket: intention, how, falsifier, decisions writes_to and bounds.in, plus git log of the files written; (3) the write door: cairn artifact write <ticket path> --verb cast --why '<what was read>' --from <file>, ensure_ascii=True; (4) what to do when there is no charter owner: open a question with cairn question open --ticket <this id>, never guess; (5) the proof path, cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_every_proved_ticket_names_its_owner.py. The ticket carries all five.
answers.children: none, because the fills are one act per ticket inside this ticket's build, each journaled through cairn artifact write, and a ticket with no charter owner becomes a question rather than a child
answers.collision_check: No real collision. Law 5 says history moves out to the commons, not that it loses its owner. The memory 'backfill writes beside without reading' is the failure this ticket is shaped against: fills are one per ticket, each read first. 3ca32dd07e86's earlier fill (data_recorder) is the worked example, not a conflict.
answers.falsifier_check: Over the live commons, no PROVED ticket's owning_intention is blank; each filled owner resolves to a charter on disk; each fill's artifact-journal line carries a why naming what was read. A fill whose why cites only the title is the failure. Horizon: the 100 at cast, every one closed by fill or by an answered question.
answers.gates_bound: code-seam@v2's prove gate: the owner proof sealed over the live commons with its hollow build retaken; on failure it feeds back to TICKETME/FIXME (Laws 3 + 8).
answers.missing_check: The 44 PROVED tickets whose owner does not resolve by a naive path check are a different defect and stay out of scope; they are recorded in measured so nothing is lost. The proof's guard must read the live commons, so it needs a resolution rule for owners (a repo-relative path under cairn/ or CairnCommons/) that is written in the proof, not assumed.
answers.questions: none, because the orchestrator's instruction (stop at TICKETME) leaves the build unstarted, and any no-charter finding opens its question at build time against this ticket; CairnCommons/questions/ is the address
